construct: RULED, THE K2 CELL (refreshed 2026-09-21): k2_overview 40–70w (the persona's current in the element's arena) + k2_functional ≤22w (the god's own family function, re-ruled 2026-09-01) + k2_domain_readings 18–55w per ruled domain (owner construct 2026-08-19, corpus ×50 LOCKED) · adj_chips {catalyst ×3, friction ×3} 1–3w under THE KEYWORD DERIVATION CHAIN (2026-09-03) and THE VOCABULARY ZONE B1–B2 (2026-09-04) · fn_reading = the weighted three-door ledger {word, doors:{trait, scene, outside}} ×3 per pole, 35–55w per door (THE THREE DOORS 2026-09-03; corpus ×50 complete 2026-09-04) · structural_interaction = the REA_03 §4b authoring seed · k2_card = the unauthored register stub (REA_03 §4, superseded by the cell above). Prompts: REA_17 §3.4. · edge (catalyst pole only; owner 2026-10-16, THE EDGE v9: two sentences, the energy and its three ruling domains from the GOD table, then a clause per domain in The Pattern's voice; the metric; the head derived in the app)

candidates.structural_interaction: Metal meeting Metal cross-polarity — similar nature, competitive register
candidates.k2_overview: Your Metal moves as the Rival: an edge that sharpens against other edges. Competition wakes you up, stakes clarify you, and you cut boldest when something real is on the table. Money and metal both change hands fast around you. The trick of your life is dueling without wounding, and betting without handing over the sword.
candidates.k2_functional: Your energy spikes for contests and crashes after. Build recovery into the schedule like a trainer would.

k2_domain_readings.Rivalry: Rivalry is your whetstone: you improve fastest with a named competitor in view. Choose rivals worth becoming, because you will absorb their shape. And retire each rivalry the day it stops sharpening and starts nicking.
k2_domain_readings.Shared stakes: You bet alongside people easily: ventures, splits, loans between friends. Metal keeps clean edges, so keep clean papers. The partnerships that survive you are the ones with terms as sharp as the trust.
k2_domain_readings.Boldness: Your nerve is surgical: boldest when the cut is clear. Practice sizing the wager to the blade. Full force is for openings that deserve it, not for every glinting chance.

angles.drive: You compete best with someone to beat and know it. Knowing where you stand matters more than comfort, so you compete harder against one rival than for any reward. Pick one contest with a finish line, because yours have no end in sight.
angles.cost_self: Without a rival, you lose your pace. Competing keeps you going, and the next round comes ahead of noticing you are tired. Compete against your own record for a month, since you never reach a finish that lets you rest.
angles.cost_others: For you, competing with a friend is taking them seriously. You raise the stakes out of wanting someone worth beating more than someone easy to keep. Keep one friend outside the contest, as you cost a rival the ease of siding with you.

angles.drive: Your yes to a bet comes before the fear has finished. Hesitating feels like losing to yourself, so you bet first and size it afterwards. Keep one bet a year you can afford to lose, since nerve costs you money as much as pride.
angles.cost_self: Whenever the stakes go up, you are first to bet. Betting first is the closest you get to sure, and you size it to nerve rather than savings. Size one bet to the savings, because the early yes costs you money put aside.
angles.cost_others: Betting first is your way of carrying the people who hesitate. By betting for the group instead of asking it, you put their money where your nerve is. Check the size with them first, before you spend their caution like your own courage.

angles.drive: You trust a person faster when the risk is shared. Sharing the risk makes the bond real to you, so you go in together ahead of writing anything down. Write the terms down once, because you risk the friendship as much as the money.
angles.cost_self: Where a friend needs backing, you share the risk first. Sharing the risk feels closer than staying out, and the shared bet comes before your margin. Keep one account no friend can draw on, since you cover their losses with money meant for rest.
angles.cost_others: Sharing a risk with someone is your warmest offer. Wanting them in it more than safe from it, you share the upside and the fall. Say the downside first, as you bring the people you like into risks sized to your nerve.

angles.drive: You keep an exact score with everyone you like. With Metal running over, you live on comparison more than company, so you keep a quiet tally of who gave more. You end up ahead on the tally and short on the company you wanted.
angles.cost_self: Whenever a friend pulls ahead, you score it as a loss rather than their win. To stay sure, you keep score and spend the friendship checking the count. You pay for every point in closeness you never collect.
angles.cost_others: Keeping the score even is how you keep a friendship honest. Since you count favours instead of simply returning them, every gift to you arrives with a price attached. Keep in mind that you wanted the closeness long before you wanted the score.

angles.drive: Your bets are sized to the thrill ahead of the margin. Metal piles up in you, so your bets run on nerve to spare and caution borrowed. You bet the rent on a feeling that fades faster than the bill.
angles.cost_self: Where the bet is biggest you are calmest, and read it as a sign. Trusting nerve more than math, you bet with the rent before the sums are done. You come out of that calm short on rent and short on sleep.
angles.cost_others: Betting the rent is how you make a thing feel real. Since you size the bet to your nerve instead of theirs, you pull the people beside you into it. You put their safety on the bet along with your own.

angles.drive: Harder than any loss deserves, you hate to lose. You read a loss to a peer as a statement about you, so you argue the result instead of taking it. You hate losing your place, if you are honest, more than losing the point.
angles.cost_self: Coming second sours the whole day for you. Being beaten feels like being replaced, and you hate the loss instead of learning from it. You give the loss the entire evening and get neither the rest nor the lesson back.
angles.cost_others: Hating to lose even a game is how you show you care. Since you want the win ahead of the evening, you keep arguing after it ends. You cost the people you play with the fun of the game.

edge.lead: Metal runs through your wealth, your social life and your career. It is the stake you put down first and count afterwards, the friendship that grows closer every time you race each other, and the pace you only find with someone ahead to catch.
